The `rcParams` in Matplotlib is a dictionary-like variable that contains the default styles for every plot element you create. The `figure.figsize` parameter within `rcParams` is used to set the default figure size for all plots. This parameter takes a tuple of two values representing the width and height of the figure in inches.

Here is an example of how to set the `figure.figsize` parameter using `rcParams`:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Set the default figure size
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (10, 6)

# Create a simple plot to see the effect
plt.plot([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6])
plt.title('Default Figure Size')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.show()
```

In this example, the figure size is set to 10 inches wide and 6 inches tall. When you run this code, the resulting plot will have the specified dimensions.

If you want to check the current value of `figure.figsize`, you can do so by accessing the `rcParams` dictionary:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Print the current figure size
print(plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'])
```

This will output the current default figure size, which might be something like:

```
(6.4, 4.8)
```

You can also reset the `figure.figsize` to its default value using:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Reset to the default figure size
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = plt.rcParamsDefault['figure.figsize']

# Create a simple plot to see the effect
plt.plot([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6])
plt.title('Default Figure Size')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.show()
```

This will revert the figure size to the default values defined by Matplotlib.
